title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Fernandez
summary: Authoritative reference for RBAC and authentication controls, end-to-end audit logging and retention, data residency requirements, Secure SDLC controls, incident response security procedures, evidence collection and packaging workflows for audits, and the risk & exceptions process. Intended for engineering, security, and compliance teams delivering or operating Redwood Inference services.
content:
Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls covering RBAC and authentication, audit logging and log retention, data residency requirements, Secure SDLC controls, incident response security procedures, evidence collection and packaging workflows for audits, and the risk/exceptions process. It is the canonical reference for engineering, security, compliance, and product teams.

Scope
Applies to: hosted API, Dedicated & Private control plane components, Redwood Console, serving runtime components, telemetry pipelines, and any auxiliary services that process customer data or control access to production infrastructure.

Ownership and contact
- Document owner: Security (owner_team)
- Primary owners: Aisha Fernandez (Security) — policy custodian; Michael Chen (Infra) — RBAC integrations; Lena Ortiz (Compliance) — evidence and audits.
- Pager: sec-oncall@redwood.example (for incidents affecting audit/logging integrity or data residency breaches)

1) RBAC & Authentication
Overview
We enforce least-privilege access through a layered RBAC model that maps corporate identities (Okta SSO / SAML) into platform roles. Service-to-service auth uses short-lived mTLS or signed tokens depending on deployment mode.

Roles and mappings (summary table)
- Organization roles (Okta groups):  redwood-admins, redwood-security, redwood-platform, redwood-sre, redwood-devs, redwood-readonly
- Platform roles: Admin, SecurityAdmin, PlatformEngineer, SRE, Developer, ReadOnly, ServiceAccount

Principles
- Least privilege: default to read-only; elevation via documented approval process.
- Separation of duties: security and platform admin functions are split where practical.
- Time-bound elevation: privileged sessions are time-limited (max 12 hours) and require MFA.

Technical controls and examples
- SSO and provisioning: Okta SCIM for group membership sync to IAM; SAML attribute mapping maps group -> platform role.
- IAM mappings: AWS IAM roles for human users are mapped to Okta groups; when using GCP/Azure, equivalent federation is required.
- Service accounts: must be registered in the service-account registry, have an owner, and use short-lived credentials minted by Vault (TTL defaults: 1 hour).
- Example SAML attribute mapping snippet (conceptual):
{
  "AttributeStatement": {
    "roles": ["redwood-platform", "redwood-devs"]
  }
}

Onboarding and offboarding
- New hires: request via HR ticket; automated provisioning creates Okta account and SCIM groups.
- Offboarding: deprovision within 4 hours for terminations; 24 hours for standard departures. Security runs a weekly orphaned-credential scan.

Auditing RBAC changes
- All group membership changes, role assignments, and policy updates are logged in audit stream (see Audit Logging). Any modification to Admin or SecurityAdmin roles triggers an alert and requires approval documented in the change log.

2) Audit logging and integrity
Logging sources
- API Gateway: request/response metadata (truncate customer payloads per PII rules).
- Serving runtime: model invocation metadata, model variant used, latency, token counts, error codes.
- Console & Admin UI: login events, role changes, policy updates, feature flags toggles.
- CI/CD and deployment pipeline: commits, pipeline runs, approvals, artifact promotions.
- Host & infra telemetry: instance lifecycle events, access to sensitive storage, Vault access logs.

Collection pipeline
1. Emit structured logs (JSON) to local aggregator (Fluentd/Vector) with enforced schema.
2. Ship to centralized ingestion (S3 (WORM)/GCS bucket + Kinesis/Streaming).
3. Index/parquet and forward to SIEM (Splunk/Datadog Security) for correlation and alerting.
4. Cold/Long-term storage: immutable archive in encrypted S3 Glacier / GCS Nearline for compliance retention windows.

Retention and retention classes (examples)
- Audit-critical logs (authentication, RBAC changes, admin actions): retention = 3 years (hot index 365 days, cold archive 3 years).
- Operational logs (runtime metrics, debug-level): retention = 90 days (unless requested for incident).
- Telemetry for billing/usage: retention = 2 years.
- SIEM derived alerts & tickets: retention = 7 years as evidence artifacts.

Integrity and monitoring
- Tamper evidence: write-once storage (WORM) for archive buckets and periodic checksum verification (SHA256) for archived segments.
- Logging gaps: missing logs or ingestion delays > 5 minutes trigger the Logging Reliability Pager. Metrics: log-latency < 1 minute 95th percentile, ingestion success >= 99.9%.
- Alerting thresholds:
  - Missing admin-action logs for > 1 hour -> Page Security Oncall (P1).
  - Unusual volume of RBAC changes (> 5 changes in 1 hour) -> Security investigation (P2).

Access to logs
- Access to raw audit logs is restricted to security and platform engineers via a dedicated role (SecurityAdmin) and requires MFA and ephemeral session tokens. Queries producing PII must use redaction functions or restricted views.

3) Data residency & retention policy
Residency rules
- Customer data residency is honored per customer contract: deployments are pinned to regions as specified in contracts (US, EU, APAC designated regions).
- Control plane metadata (non-customer-identifying) may be replicated for reliability across regions except where contract forbids.

Classification and retention matrix (examples)
- Customer PII: retention = per contract; default 90 days unless customer requests longer; deletion on demand within SLA (30 days for hosted API).
- Audit evidence: retention = 3 years.
- Usage/metrics: 2 years.
- Backups of sensitive data: encrypted, access-limited, retention = 1 year unless contract requires otherwise.

Data deletion & proof of deletion
- Deletion is an idempotent workflow that removes data from primary stores, revokes backups per retention schedules, and creates a signed deletion record (UUID + timestamp + operator). Evidence is stored in the evidence catalog for audit.
- Proof-of-deletion example: signed manifest JSON with S3 object checksums and deletion timestamps.

Export controls & third-party processors
- All third-party processors handling customer data must have a Data Processing Agreement (DPA). Processors in different regions require documented data flow diagrams and controls.

4) Secure SDLC (Secure Software Development Lifecycle)
Gates and tooling
- Code review: all PRs require 2 approvers for production-impacting changes; at least one approver must be from a different team for separation of duties.
- Static Analysis: SAST run on every PR; failing critical or high findings blocks merge.
- Dependency scanning: SCA (Dependabot/OSS scanners) with policy for automatic patching or JIRA tickets for remediation.
- Secrets detection: pre-commit hooks and runtime scanners; secrets found in repo trigger immediate rotation and incident classification.
- Infrastructure as Code: mandatory terraform fmt & validate in CI; policy-as-code (OPA/Rego) checks for network and IAM misconfigurations.

Release checklist (minimum)
1. PR approvals and passing CI (unit + integration + SAST).
2. Dependency review and risk acceptance (if necessary).
3. Canaries configured for runtime changes with rollback plan.
4. Monitoring and alerting hooks present for feature metrics.
5. Compliance artifacts updated (if feature touches data residency / PII).

Quarterly security reviews and pentests
- All internet-facing services have annual external pentests and quarterly internal red-team exercises. Critical findings must be remediated within 30 days or have a published risk exception.

5) Incident response (security procedures)
Objectives
- Contain and mitigate security incidents rapidly, preserve evidence for forensic analysis, and meet legal/regulatory notification obligations.

Incident classification
- P0 (data exfiltration or control-plane compromise) -> Immediate P1 security response and Exec notif.
- P1 (privilege escalation, credential leakage) -> Security triage and containment.
- P2 (service disruption without security impact) -> Platform incident process.

Immediate actions (first 60 minutes)
1. Triage: confirm scope and classification, identify affected services and data.
2. Containment: rotate compromised credentials, isolate impacted nodes, apply ACL changes.
3. Evidence preservation: snapshot instances (for on-prem/containerized artifacts take image / export), collect relevant logs, and lock write permissions on audit archives.
4. Notification: alert security oncall, legal, and customer-success as required by contract.

Forensics & evidence handling
- Chain of custody: record who collected artifacts, where they are stored, and ensure encryption at rest.
- Forensic images: take disk images where applicable; avoid powering off hosts unless necessary to preserve data.
- Log preservation: freeze relevant log segments; tag evidence in the evidence catalog.

Post-incident activities
- Postmortem within 7 days for P0/P1 incidents, with security-root-cause, timeline, mitigations, and action owners.
- Remediation verification: security validates fixes and re-tests.

6) Compliance evidence workflows
Evidence catalog and owners
- Evidence artifacts are stored in the Evidence Catalog (encrypted object storage with metadata index). Each artifact must have an owner, description, retention policy, and link to related control.

Common evidence types
- Access control evidence: RBAC policy snapshots, group membership exports, justification tickets for privileged access.
- Logging evidence: archive manifests, checksum proofs, SIEM snapshots for given windows.
- SDLC evidence: PR approvals, SAST reports, release checklist artifacts.
- Incident evidence: forensic reports, chain-of-custody manifests, remediation tickets.

Packaging for audits
- Standard audit package contains: control mappings (SOC2/ISO), artifacts (zipped), manifest.json (list of artifacts + checksums), owner attestations (signed PDF), and a brief executive summary.
- Evidence request SLA: security responds to internal audit requests within 5 business days; external auditors within the timeline agreed in the audit engagement letter.

Automation and attestations
- Quarterly self-attestations are auto-generated for a subset of controls (RBAC snapshots, automated config checks). Owners must confirm or provide remediation notes within 10 business days.

7) Risk, exceptions, and compensating controls
Risk acceptance process
- All risks that cannot be mitigated immediately must be documented using the Risk Acceptance Template and submitted to the Risk Committee. Required fields: risk description, impacted assets, likelihood & impact (qualitative), compensating controls, expiration date, mitigation plan, and owner.
- Approval tiers:
  - Low risk -> Security manager approval.
  - Medium risk -> Security director + Product signoff.
  - High risk -> CISO + Legal + Exec committee.

Standard compensating controls examples
- Additional monitoring & anomaly detection for services that cannot be isolated.
- Time-limited access, IP-restricted administrative windows, mandatory pair-approvals for sensitive ops.

Exception lifecycle
1. Request submitted (Risk Acceptance Template).
2. Security review & provisional approval (time-bound, e.g., 90 days).
3. Mitigation plan tracked in JIRA with owner.
4. Renewal or closure: exceptions automatically expire and must be renewed with updated justification.

Appendices
A. Operational runbook excerpts
- Log ingestion failure: check local aggregator status, backlog (fluentd/vector), network egress, S3/GCS permissions, then perform stub ingest to verify. If backlog > 2 hours, escalate to infra-pager.
- RBAC emergency revoke: steps to temporarily revoke Admin role group in Okta, confirm propagation, and record audit ID.

B. Example evidence manifest (manifest.json)
{
  "manifest_id": "evidence-2026-09-15-001",
  "owner": "Lena Ortiz",
  "items": [
    {"path": "s3://evidence/2026/q3/rbac-snapshot.json", "sha256": "..."},
    {"path": "s3://evidence/2026/q3/log-archive-20260901.parquet", "sha256": "..."}
  ]
}

C. Useful contacts and SLA summary
- Security oncall: sec-oncall@redwood.example (P0/P1)
- Audit & Compliance: compliance@redwood.example (evidence requests)
- Infra oncall: infra-oncall@redwood.example (logging pipeline issues)
- Evidence request SLA: internal=5 business days, external=as per engagement

Review cadence
- This document is reviewed quarterly by Security and Compliance and updated after each major incident or control change.
